content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

I need a box, that is on the upside open. The outer dimensions are 220 x 300 x 160mm. The wall thickness should be 8mm and the bottom thickness 12mm | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step construction strategy (function-call driven)

1. Establish the outer volume  
   • Use functions.block to create one rectangular block that represents the complete outside of the box.  
   • Parameters:  
     – x_size = 220, y_size = 300, z_size = 160 (outer dimensions)  
     – Basepoint x = 0, y = 0, z = 0.  
     – subtraction = False (this is the initial solid).

2. Hollow out the interior to form walls and leave the bottom in place  
   • Use a second entry in the same functions.block call to subtract a slightly smaller block.  
   • Wall thickness t = 8 mm; bottom thickness b = 12 mm.  
   • Inner dimensions:  
     – Inner length  = 220 – 2·t = 204 mm  
     – Inner width   = 300 – 2·t = 284 mm  
     – Inner height  = 160 – b   = 148 mm (stops at the underside of the open top)  
   • Inner block basepoint: (x = 8, y = 8, z = 12) to leave walls of 8 mm on all sides and a 12 mm bottom.  
   • subtraction = True so this volume is removed.

3. No other geometries (cylinders, forces) are needed, so after the two block specifications we will finish with functions.finished.

Parameter arrays to be supplied (corresponding entries align across arrays):
x_size        [220, 204]  
y_size        [300, 284]  
z_size        [160, 148]  
x             [  0,   8]  
y             [  0,   8]  
z             [  0,  12]  
subtraction   [False, True]

When you are ready, ask me to prepare the actual function-call JSON; I will supply it exactly as described.

Now i want you to execute the prepared function calls one after the other. If you need to do some calculations or geometrical algebra, use the CreateCode Function first. Execute the first prepared function call. Submit all required variables at once
successfully created block object. Call now the next function!
